## Adapter-contract decision record — task 12890 (2026-11-08)

**Current-state re-verification:** issue [#5803](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5803) remains open. Parent [#5672](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5672) is now **closed**: its latest closure record says its decomposition acceptance was met and the child designs continue independently ([closure evidence](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5672#issuecomment-6728213156)). This decision applies the parent's Part B adapter framing and its selective-grant/existence-privacy constraints; it does **not** change the parent's grants, revocation, delegation, or privacy decisions. The fuller companion record is in [PR #7739](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7739) (still open; not represented as merged).

### Chosen shared contract

- **Addressing:** every exposed foreign collection has a stable ID-level reference of the form `id://foreign/<adapter-id>/<source-alias>/<resource-path>`. The alias resolves only in owner-local endpoint configuration; adapter-native locators (origins, URLs, database paths) and secret-bearing URL parts are not embedded in shared ID references. Resource paths are adapter-canonical, versioned, and may not collapse distinct source collections. Only owner-selected collections are exposed.
- **Type mapping:** each adapter publishes a versioned, explicit mapping into the common ID vocabulary: null, boolean, signed 64-bit integer, finite float64, UTF-8 string, bytes, UTC-microsecond timestamp, ordered list, string-keyed record, and namespaced/versioned tagged values where a source type must remain distinct (for example, out-of-range BigInt). No implicit coercion or silent field/record loss: unsupported or lossy values are rejected or reported with a typed loss report. A decimal string alone is not a lossless BigInt mapping unless the mapped schema explicitly tags it as such.
- **Live vs. materialized:** adapters declare supported modes; the owner chooses an allowed mode per collection. Adapter-specific defaults are explicit (or configuration is required). Live reads have bounded deadlines and report observation/consistency; failures do not become empty results or silently fall back to stale snapshots. Materializations are bounded before copy, atomically replaced, and carry source/schema/mapping version, time, completeness, and loss provenance. Cross-source atomicity is never implied.
- **Direction and credentials:** v1 is read-only against foreign stores; materialization is an ID-side copy, not write-back. A local opaque credential reference may resolve to a least-privilege secret at call time; raw credentials and secret-bearing locators never enter ID data, grants, references, snapshots, logs, traces, or errors. A grant provides access only to the selected ID data, never the source credential.
- **Failure/privacy:** outcomes are stable and typed; partial/truncated results are marked and never presented as complete. Queries that cannot enforce the caller's grant at the source are refused rather than fetched broadly and filtered afterward. Grantee-visible responses collapse distinctions (including not-granted vs. not-found vs. unavailable) whenever they could reveal withheld existence or shape. This exact error-collapse choice is a conservative adapter policy: #5672 leaves that particular distinction open, so this record does not claim it was already settled at parent level.

### Candidate and alternative dispositions

IndexedDB, Postgres-over-HTTP, Turso/libsql HTTP, and Redis/SQLite remain adapter-specific designs under their existing child tickets; each supplies its own supported query shapes, mode/default, mapping/loss cases, limits, and failure semantics while conforming to the shared contract. **p2panda is deferred, not accepted as a v1 table adapter.** The routed candidate is a distinct local-first/P2P protocol and append-only-log ecosystem with its own schema and identity surfaces; the issues establish no shared schema or concrete cross-ecosystem consumer. ID's native journal also means compatibility must not be inferred from the historical iroh-docs motivation. Revisit only with a named interop use case and explicit schema, identity, grant, and loss mapping; a one-shot export/conversion is also deferred until it has a concrete consumer.

Rejected alternatives: adapter-invented shareable URI schemes (inconsistent identity/grant/privacy boundaries); physical locators or credentials in ID references (replication and disclosure risk); universal coercion (silent semantic loss); requiring every adapter to be live-only or materialize-only (source capabilities differ); and unrestricted raw query/write passthrough (can escape grants/limits and exceeds read-only v1).

### Implementation invariants
